newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea opposition rejects Kim apology, vows fight.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea opposition rejects Kim apology, vows fight.

text.p: South Korea's main opposition party on Friday dismissed President Kim Young-sam's apology over election spending abuses, and vowed to fight to reveal the truth.
"President Kim's speech ended by avoiding and shifting all responsibility," said a spokeswoman for the National Congress for New Politics. "We will use all means to fight to reveal the truth."
The opposition alleges that Kim's 1992 presidential campaign was partly bankrolled by the scandal-ridden Hanbo Group and far exceeded legal spending limits.

"We will try to call President Kim Young-sam to a National Assembly hearing as a witness," spokeswoman Park Sun-suck said, adding that her party would join hands with the smaller United Liberal Democrats to put pressure on Kim.
Earlier, Kim apologised on national television for past campaign spending abuses by himself and others and called for reform legislation.
But he offered no specifics that could incriminate him.
